mishnayos.summary: The firstborn of a donkey must be redeemed, but only if it belongs fully to a Jew. If a non-Jew owns any part of it, or if it belongs to Kohanim or Levi'im, it does not have the halachos of a bechor.

chunks.en: Someone who buys the unborn baby of a non-Jew's donkey,
chunks.st: With regard to one who purchases the fetus of a donkey that belongs to a gentile,

chunks.he: וְהַמּוֹכֵר לוֹ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי,
chunks.en: or sells his donkey's unborn baby to a non-Jew, even though he is not allowed to,
chunks.st: and one who sells the fetus of his donkey to a gentile although he is not permitted to sell a large animal to a gentile,

words.note: Chazal did not let a Jew sell a big work animal to a non-Jew.

chunks.en: or becomes partners with a non-Jew in a donkey,
chunks.st: and one who enters into a partnership with
chunks.stMore: a gentile in ownership of a donkey or its fetus,

chunks.en: or takes a donkey from a non-Jew to care for it and share the babies,
chunks.st: and one who receives a donkey from
chunks.stMore: a gentile in order to care for it in exchange for partnership in its offspring,

chunks.en: or gives his donkey to a non-Jew to care for it in that way,
chunks.st: and one who gives his donkey to a gentile in receivership,

chunks.en: in all of these cases, the baby donkey is not a bechor.
chunks.st: in all of these cases the donkeys are exempt from the obligations of firstborn status,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they do not have firstborn status and are not redeemed,

words.note: A bechor is a firstborn. A firstborn donkey must be redeemed by giving a lamb to a Kohen.

chunks.en: Because the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "the firstborns in Yisrael," but not those of others.
chunks.st: “I sanctified to Me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and animal” (Numbers 3:13), indicating that the mitzva is incumbent upon the Jewish people, but not upon others.
chunks.stMore: If the firstborn belongs even partially to a gentile, it does not have firstborn status.

chunks.en: Kohanim and Levi'im do not have to redeem a firstborn donkey; we learn it from a kal vachomer:
chunks.st: Priests and Levites are exempt from the obligation to redeem a firstborn donkey; this is derived from an a fortiori
chunks.stMore: inference: In the wilderness the firstborn were redeemed in exchange for the Levites, as it is stated: “Take the Levites in exchange for all the firstborn among the children of Israel and the animal of the Levites in exchange for their animals” (Numbers 3:45).

words.note: A kal vachomer is a proof that goes from an easier case to a harder case.

chunks.en: In the midbar, the Levi'im took the place of the firstborns of the rest of Yisrael,
chunks.st: If the priests and Levites rendered exempt the firstborn children and donkeys of the Israelites in the wilderness from being counted firstborns,

chunks.en: so surely they should free their own firstborns.
chunks.st: it is only logical that the priests and the Levites should render the firstborn of their own donkeys exempt from being counted firstborns.

chunks.st: consumption of the non-kosher fish is prohibited

chunks.st: and the Sages penalized the seller in that he must return the money to them, which they paid for the meat that they ate.

chunks.en: And what they did not eat:
chunks.st: And with regard to that which they did not eat,

chunks.en: the meat must be buried,
chunks.st: that meat must be buried,

chunks.en: and he must give them back the money.
chunks.st: and he must return the money
chunks.stMore: that they paid for the meat that they did not eat.

chunks.en: The same if someone shechted a cow
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of one who slaughters a cow

chunks.en: and sold it, and they found out it was treif:
chunks.st: and sells it, and it was discovered that it is a tereifa,

words.note: An animal with a deadly injury, which may not be eaten.

chunks.he: מַה שֶׁאָכְלוּ אָכְלוּ וְיַחֲזִיר לָהֶם אֶת הַדָּמִים.
chunks.en: what they ate, they ate, and he must give them back the money.
chunks.st: what the buyers ate, they ate,

chunks.en: And what they did not eat:
chunks.st: and what they did not eat,

chunks.en: they give him back the meat,
chunks.st: they must return the meat to
chunks.stMore: the seller, who may sell it to a gentile or feed it to the dogs,

chunks.en: and he gives them back the money.
chunks.st: and he must return the money to the buyers.

chunks.en: If they sold it to non-Jews or threw it to the dogs,
chunks.st: If the buyers sold it to gentiles or cast it to the dogs,

chunks.en: they must pay him what treif meat is worth.
chunks.st: they pay the seller the value of a tereifa,
chunks.stMore: which is less than the value of kosher meat, and the seller refunds the balance to the buyers.

mishnayos.summary: This perek lists the blemishes that let us shecht a bechor outside the Beis HaMikdash. It begins with blemishes of the ear.

chunks.he: עַל אֵלּוּ מוּמִין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר,
chunks.en: For these blemishes we may shecht a bechor:
chunks.st: For these blemishes, one may slaughter the firstborn animal outside the Temple: If the firstborn’s

chunks.en: if a piece is missing from the hard part of its ear,
chunks.st: ear was damaged and lacking from the cartilage [haḥasḥus],

chunks.en: but not just from the skin,
chunks.st: but not if the skin was damaged;

chunks.he: נִסְדְּקָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא חָסְרָה,
chunks.en: if the ear was split, even if nothing is missing,
chunks.st: and likewise, if the ear was split, although it is not lacking;

chunks.en: if it has a hole the size of a bean,
chunks.st: or if the ear was pierced with a hole the size of a bitter vetch, which is a type of legume;

words.note: A small kind of bean called karshinah.

chunks.en: or if it dried up.
chunks.st: or if it was an ear that is desiccated.

chunks.en: What is a dried-up ear?
chunks.st: What is a desiccated ear that is considered a blemish? It is

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁתִּנָּקֵב וְאֵינָהּ מוֹצִיאָה טִפַּת דָּם.
chunks.en: Any ear that gives out no drop of blood when it is pricked.
chunks.st: any ear that if it is pierced it does not discharge a drop of blood.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:

chunks.en: dried up means that it crumbles.
chunks.st: Desiccated means that the ear is so dry that it will crumble if one touches it.

mishnayos.summary: Blemishes of the eye that let us shecht a bechor.

chunks.en: An eyelid that has a hole in it,
chunks.st: The eyelid that was pierced,

chunks.en: that is damaged, or that is split,
chunks.st: an eyelid that was damaged and is lacking, or an eyelid that was split;
chunks.stMore: and likewise, one may slaughter a firstborn animal outside the Temple

chunks.en: or if its eye has a thin cloud,
chunks.st: if there was in his eye a cataract,

chunks.en: a tevallul, or a growth shaped like a snail, a snake, or a grape.
chunks.st: a tevallul, or a growth in the shape of a snail, a snake, or a berry that covers the pupil.

chunks.en: What is a tevallul?
chunks.st: What is a tevallul?

chunks.en: A white line that crosses the ring of the eye and goes into the black.
chunks.st: It is a white thread that bisects the iris and enters the black pupil.

chunks.en: If it is black and goes into the white,
chunks.st: If it is a black thread that bisects the iris and enters the white of the eye

chunks.en: it is not a blemish, because blemishes in the white part do not count.
chunks.st: it is not a blemish.

mishnayos.stIntro: For these blemishes of the eye, one may slaughter the firstborn animal outside the Temple:

mishnayos.summary: More eye blemishes: pale spots and tears that do not go away. The mishnah explains how we know they will not go away.

chunks.en: Pale spots on the eye, and tears that do not stop.
chunks.st: Pale spots on the eye and tears streaming from the eye that are constant
chunks.stMore: are blemishes that enable the slaughter of the firstborn.

chunks.en: Which pale spots are lasting?
chunks.st: Which are the pale spots that are constant?

chunks.en: Any that stayed eighty days.
chunks.st: They are any spots that persisted for eighty days.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥananya ben Antigonus said:

chunks.he: בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ שְׁלשָׁה פְעָמִים בְּתוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם.
chunks.en: we check it three times within eighty days.
chunks.st: One examines it three times within eighty days.
chunks.stMore: Only if the spots are found during all three examinations are they considered constant.

chunks.en: And these are lasting tears:
chunks.st: And these are the constant tears,
chunks.stMore: i.e., this is how it is known whether the blemish is temporary or permanent:

chunks.en: if it ate fresh and dry grass from a field watered by rain,
chunks.st: In a case where the animal ate, for medicinal purposes, moist fodder and dry fodder from a field watered exclusively with rain,

chunks.en: or fresh and dry grass from a field watered by streams,
chunks.st: or if the animal ate moist fodder and dry fodder from an irrigated field,

chunks.he: אָכַל הַיָּבֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָכַל הַלַּח,
chunks.en: if it ate the dry and then ate the fresh,
chunks.st: or even if the animal did not eat them together but ate the dry fodder and thereafter ate the moist
chunks.stMore: fodder, and the condition of constant tears was not healed,

chunks.en: it is not a blemish,
chunks.st: it is not a blemish.

chunks.en: unless it eats the dry after the fresh and the tears do not stop.
chunks.st: It is not a blemish unless the animal eats the moist fodder and thereafter eats the dry fodder and is not thereby healed.

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes of a bechor: of the nose, the lips and the gums.

chunks.en: Its nose that has a hole, or is damaged, or is split,
chunks.st: Its nose that was pierced, or that was damaged and is lacking, or that was split.

chunks.en: its lip that has a hole, or is damaged, or is split,
chunks.st: Likewise, its lip that was pierced, or that was damaged, or that was split
chunks.stMore: is considered a blemish. The mishna lists additional blemishes that permit the slaughter of the firstborn:

chunks.en: its outer gums that are damaged or scraped,
chunks.st: The external gums that were damaged and lacking or that were scratched,

chunks.en: and its inner gums that were pulled out.
chunks.st: and likewise, the internal gums that were extracted.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

chunks.en: we do not check from the double teeth and further in,
chunks.st: One does not examine from the double teeth, i.e., the large molars that appear like two teeth, and inward,

chunks.en: and not even the double teeth themselves.
chunks.st: and one does not examine even the place of the double teeth
chunks.stMore: themselves. This is because even if they were extracted, it is a concealed blemish, and it does not permit the slaughter of the firstborn.

mishnayos.stIntro: For these additional blemishes, one may slaughter a firstborn animal outside the Temple:

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes of a bechor: of private parts of the body, and of the tail.

chunks.he: נִפְגַּם הַזּוֹבָן, אוֹ עֶרְיָה שֶׁל נְקֵבָּה בַּמֻּקְדָּשִׁים,
chunks.en: If a hidden part of its body is damaged,
if the tail was damaged at the bone,
but not at the joint,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה רֹאשׁ הַזָּנָב מַפְצִיל עֶצֶם,
chunks.en: or if the tip of the tail is split open to the bone,
or if there is flesh between
one bone of the tail and the next, a full finger wide.

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes of a bechor's body, and how Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva say to check them.

chunks.en: If it is missing a part of its body,
or it has only one of them.
Rabbi Yishmael says,
if it has two pouches,
it has both parts.
If it has only one pouch,
it has only one part.
Rabbi Akiva says,
we sit it down on its back end and press,
if the part is there,
in the end it will come out.
Once someone pressed and it did not come out,
and the animal was shechted, and it was found stuck inside,
Rabbi Akiva allowed it, but
and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri forbade it.

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes of a bechor: of the legs and the hips.

chunks.en: An animal with five legs,
chunks.st: An animal with five legs,

chunks.en: or that has only three,
chunks.st: or one that has only three,

chunks.en: or whose hooves are closed like a donkey's,
chunks.st: or one whose hooves on its legs were closed like those of a donkey and not split,

chunks.en: or a shachul, or a kasul.
chunks.st: or the shaḥul, or the kasul may be slaughtered.

chunks.en: What is a shachul?
chunks.st: What is a shaḥul? It is an animal with

chunks.en: One whose hip bone slipped out of place.
chunks.st: a thighbone that was dislocated.

chunks.en: And a kasul is one whose one hip is higher than the other.
chunks.st: And what is a kasul? It is an animal whose build is asymmetrical in that one of its thighs is higher than the other.

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes: a broken leg bone. Ila listed all these blemishes in Yavneh, and he added three more that a later beis din agreed to.

chunks.en: If the bone of its front leg was broken,
chunks.st: the bone of its foreleg

chunks.he: וְעֶצֶם רַגְלוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִכָּר.
chunks.en: or the bone of its back leg, even though it does not show.
chunks.st: or the bone of its hind leg was broken, even though it is not conspicuous.

chunks.en: These blemishes Ila listed in Yavneh,
chunks.st: With regard to these blemishes listed in this chapter, Ila, who was expert in blemishes of the firstborn, enumerated them in Yavne,

chunks.en: and the Sages agreed with him.
chunks.st: and the Sages deferred to his expertise.

chunks.en: And he added three more.
chunks.st: And Ila added three additional blemishes,

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: and the Sages said to him:

chunks.en: "We did not hear of these."
chunks.st: We did not hear about those.

chunks.he: אֵת שֶׁגַּלְגַּל עֵינוֹ עָגוֹל כְּשֶׁל אָדָם,
chunks.en: One whose eyeball is round like a person's,
chunks.st: Ila added: An animal whose eye is round like that of a person,

chunks.en: and whose mouth looks like a pig's,
chunks.st: or whose mouth is similar to that of a pig,

chunks.en: and one that lost most of the talking part of its tongue.
chunks.st: or where most of the segment of its tongue corresponding to the segment that facilitates speech in the tongue of a person was removed.

chunks.en: The beis din after them said,
chunks.st: The court that followed them said with regard to each of those three blemishes:

chunks.en: these are blemishes.
chunks.st: That is a blemish that enables the slaughter of the firstborn.

mishnayos.stIntro: Additional blemishes that permit the slaughter of the firstborn include those where

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes: a jaw that sticks out, a doubled ear, and a tail like a pig's.

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהַלְּחִי הַתַּחְתּוֹן עוֹדֵף עַל הָעֶלְיוֹן,
chunks.en: Once the lower jaw stuck out past the upper one.
chunks.st: And there was an incident where the lower jaw of the firstborn protruded beyond the upper jaw,

chunks.he: וְשָׁלַח רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים וְאָמְרוּ,
chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel sent to ask the Sages, and they said,
chunks.st: and Rabban Gamliel asked the Sages for a ruling, and they said:

chunks.en: "This is a blemish."
chunks.st: That is a blemish that enables the slaughter of the firstborn.

chunks.en: A young goat's ear that was doubled:
chunks.st: With regard to the ear of the kid that was doubled and appeared like two ears,

chunks.en: the Sages said,
chunks.st: the Sages said:

chunks.en: when it is one bone, it is a blemish.
chunks.st: When the additional ear is one bone, i.e., it has its own cartilage, it is a blemish;

chunks.he: וְאִם אֵינָהּ עֶצֶם אֶחָד, אֵינָהּ מוּם.
chunks.en: And if it is not one bone, it is not a blemish.
chunks.st: when it does not have its own bone it is not a blemish.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chananya ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥananya ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: זְנַב הַגְּדִי שֶׁהִיא דוֹמָה לְשֶׁל חֲזִיר,
chunks.en: a young goat's tail that looks like a pig's,
chunks.st: In the case of the tail of a kid that is similar to that of a pig

chunks.en: or that does not have three joints,
chunks.st: or one that is so short that it does not have three joints,

chunks.en: this is a blemish.
chunks.st: that is a blemish.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus lists more blemishes. Rabbi Yehudah adds one more, but the Sages do not agree.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
one with a wart in its eye,
one whose front leg bone or back leg bone was damaged,
and one whose jaw bone came loose.
One eye big and one small,
one ear big and one small,
when you can see it, but not if you must measure it.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
if one body part is twice as big as the other, it is a blemish,
and the Sages did not agree with him.

mishnayos.summary: A calf's tail that is too short is a blemish. These are all the blemishes that let us shecht a bechor and redeem unfit holy animals.

chunks.en: A calf's tail that does not reach the knee joint:
chunks.st: In the case of the tail of a calf that does not reach the leg joint [la’arkov],

chunks.en: the Sages said,
chunks.st: the Sages said: It is a blemish,

chunks.en: most calves are like this:
chunks.st: because all growth of calves is in this manner:

chunks.he: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהֵן מַגְדִּילִין הֵם נִמְתָּחוֹת.
chunks.en: as long as they grow, their tails stretch.
chunks.st: As long as they grow, their tails are extended beneath the leg joint.

chunks.en: Which joint did they mean?
chunks.st: Which is the leg joint about which the Sages spoke?

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

chunks.en: the joint in the middle of the leg.
chunks.st: They are referring to the leg joint that is in the middle of the thigh.

words.en: that is in the middle of

chunks.he: עַל אֵלּוּ מוּמִין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַבְּכוֹר,
chunks.en: For these blemishes we may shecht a bechor,
chunks.st: For these blemishes enumerated in the previous mishnayot, one slaughters the firstborn outside the Temple

chunks.en: and unfit holy animals are redeemed because of them.
chunks.st: and disqualified consecrated animals may be redeemed on their account.

mishnayos.summary: These are problems that do not let us shecht a bechor, neither in the Beis HaMikdash nor outside it. The Rabbis argue about an animal whose body is not clearly male or female.

chunks.en: These are blemishes we do not shecht for,
not in the Beis HaMikdash and not in the rest of the land:
pale spots and tears that do not last,
and inner gums that were damaged,
but not pulled out,
and one with sores,
and one with warts,
and one with a rash,
an old one, a sick one,
a smelly one, and one that was used for a sin,
and one that killed a person,
when only one witness
or the owner says so,
and an animal whose body is not clearly male or female,
not in the Beis HaMikdash and not in the rest of the land.
Rabbi Yishmael says,
there is no blemish bigger than this.
But the Sages say,
it is not a bechor,
so it may be sheared and used for work.

mishnayos.summary: The blemishes that make an animal unfit for a korban also stop a Kohen from doing the avodah. A Kohen has some extra blemishes too, like an oddly shaped head.

chunks.en: These blemishes,
chunks.st: Concerning these blemishes which were taught with regard to an animal,

chunks.en: whether they last or pass,
chunks.st: whether they are permanent or transient,

chunks.en: make a person unfit too.
chunks.st: they also disqualify in the case of a person,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they disqualify a priest from performing the Temple service.

chunks.en: More than these, for a person:
chunks.st: And in addition to those
chunks.stMore: blemishes, there are other blemishes that apply only to a priest:

chunks.en: one whose head is pointed, or shaped like a turnip,
chunks.st: One whose head is pointed, narrow above and wide below; and one whose head is turnip-like, wide above and narrow below;

chunks.en: one whose head is like a hammer, or has a dent, or sticks out in back.
chunks.st: and one whose head is hammer-like, with his forehead protruding; and one whose head has an indentation; and one wherein the back of his head protrudes.

chunks.en: A Kohen with a hunched back:
chunks.st: And with regard to those with humped backs,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says he is fit,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda deems them fit for service

chunks.en: and the Sages say he is unfit.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem them disqualified.

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes of a Kohen: hair around the head, eyebrows, and the back.

chunks.en: A bald Kohen is unfit.
chunks.st: The kere’aḥ is disqualified from performing the Temple service.

chunks.en: Who is called bald?
chunks.st: What is a kere’aḥ?

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שִׁטָּה שֶׁל שֵׂעָר
chunks.en: Anyone who does not have a line of hair
chunks.st: It is anyone who does not have a row of hair

chunks.en: going around from ear to ear.
chunks.st: encircling his head from ear to ear.

chunks.en: If he has it,
chunks.st: If he has a row of hair from ear to ear,

chunks.en: he is fit.
chunks.st: that person is fit for service.

chunks.en: If he has no eyebrows,
chunks.st: If a priest has no eyebrows,

chunks.en: or he has only one eyebrow,
chunks.st: or if he has only one eyebrow,

chunks.en: he is the "gibben" that the Torah talks about.
chunks.st: that is the gibben that is stated in the Torah
chunks.stMore: in the list of blemished priests (see Leviticus 21:20).

chunks.en: Rabbi Dosa says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Dosa says:

chunks.en: anyone whose eyebrows lie flat over his eyes.
chunks.st: A gibben is one whose eyebrows are so long that they lie flat and cover his eyes.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי גַבִּים וּשְׁתֵּי שִׁדְרָאוֹת:
chunks.en: anyone who has two backs and two backbones.
chunks.st: A gibben is one who has two backs and two spines.

mishnayos.summary: Blemishes of a Kohen's eyes and nose.

chunks.en: A charum is unfit.
chunks.st: The ḥarum is disqualified from performing the Temple service.

chunks.en: Who is a charum?
chunks.st: What is a ḥarum?

chunks.en: One who can paint both his eyes at once, with one stroke.
chunks.st: It is one who can paint both of his eyes as one,
chunks.stMore: with one brushstroke, because he has a sunken nose.

chunks.en: Both his eyes are high up,
chunks.st: If both of one’s eyes are above

chunks.en: or both his eyes are low,
chunks.st: or both of his eyes are below;

chunks.en: one eye is high
chunks.st: or if one of his eyes is above

chunks.en: and one eye is low,
chunks.st: and one of his eyes is below;

chunks.he: רוֹאֶה אֶת הַחֶדֶר וְאֶת הָעֲלִיָּה כְּאֶחָת,
chunks.en: he sees the room downstairs and the upstairs at the same time,
chunks.st: or if both eyes are in the proper place but he sees both the room on the ground floor and the upper story as one, at the same time;

chunks.en: one who cannot look at the sun,
chunks.st: and likewise those unable to look at the sun;

chunks.en: one whose eyes are different, and one whose eyes always tear,
chunks.st: and one whose eyes are different; and one whose eyes tear constantly,
chunks.stMore: these are disqualified from performing the Temple service.

words.note: One eye a different color from the other.
One whose eyes always run with tears.

chunks.en: And one whose eyelashes fell out
chunks.st: And one whose eyelashes have fallen out

chunks.en: is unfit because of how it looks.
chunks.st: is disqualified from performing the Temple service due to the appearance
chunks.stMore: of a blemish. Unlike the others listed in this mishna, who are disqualified by Torah law, one with this condition is not disqualified by Torah law. Rather, the Sages issued a decree prohibiting a priest with such a condition to perform the Temple service.

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes of a Kohen: eyes, body, nose and ears that are too big or too small.

chunks.en: His eyes are big like a calf's,
chunks.st: eyes are large like those of a calf

chunks.en: or small like a goose's,
chunks.st: or small like those of a goose; if

chunks.he: גּוּפוֹ גָּדוֹל מֵאֵבָרָיו אוֹ קָטָן מֵאֵבָרָיו,
chunks.en: his body is too big or too small for his limbs,
chunks.st: his body is disproportionately large relative to his limbs or disproportionately small relative to his limbs; if

chunks.he: חָטְמוֹ גָּדוֹל מֵאֵבָרָיו אוֹ קָטָן מֵאֵבָרָיו,
chunks.en: his nose is too big or too small for his limbs,
chunks.st: his nose is disproportionately large relative to his limbs or disproportionately small relative to his limbs, he is disqualified. And

chunks.en: the tzimem and the tzimei'a.
chunks.st: the tzomem and the tzome’a are also disqualified.

chunks.en: Who is a tzimei'a?
chunks.st: What is a tzome’a?

chunks.en: One whose ears are small.
chunks.st: It is anyone whose ears are small.

chunks.en: And the tzimem is one whose ears look like a sponge.
chunks.st: And what is the tzomem? It is anyone whose ears are similar to a sponge.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna lists additional blemishes that disqualify a priest from performing the Temple service: If a priest’s

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes of a Kohen, of the lips, teeth and body. The Rabbis argue about the meaning of one blemish named in the Torah.

chunks.en: If his upper lip sticks out over the lower one,
or the lower sticks out over the upper,
this is a blemish.
One whose teeth were taken out
is unfit because of how it looks.
One whose chest sags,
one whose belly is swollen,
one whose belly button sticks out,
one who has fits, even once in a long while,
one who gets a sad, gloomy mood,
and one with a body part that is too big.

words.en: the one with a big part

chunks.en: If he is missing a body part,

chunks.he: אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵיצָה אַחַת,
chunks.en: or he has only one,
this is the "mero'ach ashech" that the Torah talks about.
Rabbi Yishmael says,
anyone whose body part was crushed.
Rabbi Akiva says,
anyone whose body part is swollen.
Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
anyone whose looks are dark.

mishnayos.summary: More blemishes of a Kohen's legs, feet and fingers. Some problems make a Kohen unfit but not an animal.

chunks.en: One whose ankles or knees knock together,
chunks.st: knock his ankles or his knees into each other as he walks,

chunks.en: one with a bump, and one with bowed legs.
chunks.st: and a ba’al happikim, and the ikkel.

chunks.en: Who is bow-legged?
chunks.st: What is the ikkel?

chunks.en: Anyone who puts his feet together
chunks.st: It is anyone who places his feet together

chunks.en: and his knees do not touch each other.
chunks.st: and his knees do not knock into each other, i.e., he is bowlegged.

chunks.en: A bump that sticks out from his big toe,
chunks.st: A priest with a protuberance emerging alongside the thumb of his hand or the big toe of his foot,

chunks.en: his heel sticks out to the back,
chunks.st: or one whose heel emerges and protrudes back from his foot,

chunks.en: his foot is wide like a goose's.
chunks.st: or one whose feet are wide like those of a goose
chunks.stMore: are all disqualified from performing the Temple service.

chunks.en: His fingers lie on top of each other,
chunks.st: A priest whose fingers or toes are configured one upon the other,

chunks.en: or are stuck together.
chunks.st: or one whose fingers or toes are attached, is likewise disqualified.

chunks.en: If only up to the joint, he is fit.
chunks.st: But if they were attached from above the palm of the hand or the bottom of the foot only until the middle joint, he is fit.

chunks.en: If they were stuck below the joint and he cut them apart, he is fit.
chunks.st: If they were attached below the joint, higher up on the finger or toe, and he cut to separate them, he is fit.

chunks.en: If he had an extra finger and cut it off:
chunks.st: In a case where there was an extra finger or toe on his hand or foot and he cut it,

chunks.en: if it has a bone, he is unfit,
chunks.st: if that extra appendage contains a bone, the priest is disqualified even after it was cut,

chunks.en: and if not, he is fit.
chunks.st: and if there is no bone the priest is fit.

chunks.he: יָתֵר בְּיָדָיו וּבְרַגְלָיו שֵׁשׁ וָשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע,
chunks.en: If he has extra fingers and toes on his hands and feet, six and six, twenty-four in all,
chunks.st: If there was an extra appendage on his hands and on his feet, six on each for a total of twenty-four,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says he is fit,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda deems the priest fit

chunks.en: and the Sages say he is unfit.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem him disqualified.

chunks.en: One who uses both hands equally:
chunks.st: With regard to one who is ambidextrous and has control of both of his hands,

chunks.en: Rebbi says he is unfit,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi deems the priest disqualified,
chunks.stMore: as his halakhic status is like that of one who is left-handed,

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi.

chunks.en: and the Sages say he is fit.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem him fit.

chunks.en: One with very dark skin, one with very red skin,
chunks.st: Concerning the kushi, the giḥor,

chunks.en: one with very white skin, one who is very tall,
chunks.st: the lavkan, the kipe’aḥ,

chunks.en: a very short person, one who cannot hear or speak,
chunks.st: the dwarf, the deaf-mute,

chunks.en: one who is not mentally fit, one who is drunk,
chunks.st: the imbecile, the drunk,

chunks.en: and one with tahor tzara'as marks:
chunks.st: and those with ritually pure marks,

chunks.en: these make a person unfit,
chunks.st: their conditions disqualify a person from performing the Temple service

chunks.en: but are fine in an animal.
chunks.st: and are valid, i.e., they do not disqualify with regard to being sacrificed, in the case of an animal.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: an animal that is not fit in its mind is not the best.
chunks.st: An imbecile among animals is not optimal for sacrifice.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: also those with hanging skin or flesh
chunks.st: Even with regard to those with flesh or skin that hangs from their body,

chunks.en: are unfit in a person,
chunks.st: that blemish disqualifies in the case of a person

chunks.en: and fit in an animal.
chunks.st: and is valid in the case of an animal.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna lists additional blemishes that disqualify a priest from performing the Temple service: One whose legs are crooked and bend inward, causing him to

mishnayos.summary: Some things make an animal unfit for a korban but not a Kohen. A Kohen who did certain sins may not do the avodah until he promises to stop.

chunks.en: These are fit in a person
but unfit in an animal:
an animal and its child shechted on the same day,
a treifah, and one born through its mother's side,
one that was used for a sin, and one that killed a person.
A Kohen who marries women he may not marry
is unfit until he makes a neder not to get any benefit from her.
A Kohen who makes himself tamei to the dead
is unfit until he takes upon himself that he will not
become tamei to the dead again.

mishnayos.summary: A firstborn son can be a bechor for getting a double share of the inheritance, for pidyon haben with a Kohen, for both, or for neither. The mishnah gives examples of each.

chunks.he: יֵשׁ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵינוֹ בְכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן,
chunks.en: Some are a bechor for inheritance but not a bechor for the Kohen,
some are a bechor for the Kohen but not for inheritance,
some are a bechor for inheritance and for the Kohen,

chunks.he: יֵשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְכוֹר לֹא לַנַּחֲלָה וְלֹא לַכֹּהֵן.
chunks.en: and some are not a bechor, not for inheritance and not for the Kohen.

chunks.he: אֵיזֶהוּ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵינוֹ בְכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן,
chunks.en: Who is a bechor for inheritance but not for the Kohen?

chunks.he: הַבָּא אַחַר הַנְּפָלִים שֶׁיָּצָא רֹאשׁוֹ חַי,
chunks.en: One born after an earlier baby that did not live, even if it came out alive at first,

words.en: the ones that did not live

chunks.en: or after a full-term baby that did not live,
or after a birth that looked like an animal or a bird.
That is what Rabbi Meir says.
But the Sages say,
only if it had the shape of a person.
A woman who lost an unformed baby or a birth sac,

words.note: A shapeless birth that looks like a flat fish.

chunks.en: or a sac with a forming baby, or one that came out in parts:

words.en: and the one that comes out

chunks.en: the one born after them
is a bechor for inheritance but not for the Kohen.
A man who had no sons
married a woman who already had a child,
or she had it while still a maidservant and then was freed,
or while still a non-Jew and then became a giyores,
and once she joined Yisrael she had a son:
he is a bechor for inheritance but not for the Kohen.
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says,
he is a bechor for inheritance and for the Kohen,
as the pasuk says,
"every first one born among Bnei Yisrael,"

words.note: Literally "the one that opens the womb."

chunks.en: which means the first child born to a Jewish mother.
A man who had sons
and married a woman who never had a child,
or she became a giyores or was freed while expecting,
or she and a Kohen's wife gave birth, or she and a Levi's wife,
or she and a woman who already had a child, and the babies got mixed up,

chunks.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁהֲתָה אַחַר בַּעְלָהּ
chunks.en: and also a woman who did not wait after her husband died
three months, and married again and had a baby,

chunks.he: וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אִם בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה לָרִאשׁוֹן,
chunks.en: and we do not know if he was born after nine months to the first husband,
or after seven months to the second:
he is a bechor for the Kohen but not for inheritance.
Who is a bechor for inheritance and for the Kohen?
A son born after his mother lost a sac with no baby in it,
full of water or full of pieces,

chunks.he: הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים,
chunks.en: or lost something shaped like fish, grasshoppers or crawling creatures,
or lost a baby on the fortieth day:
the son born after them
is a bechor for inheritance and for the Kohen.

mishnayos.summary: A baby born through a cut in his mother's side, and the one born after him: Rabbi Shimon says each one counts as a bechor in a different way.

chunks.en: A baby born through his mother's side, and the one born after him:
chunks.st: In the case of a boy born by caesarean section and the son who follows him,

chunks.he: שְׁנֵיהֶם אֵינָן בְּכוֹר לֹא לַנַּחֲלָה וְלֹא לַכֹּהֵן.
chunks.en: neither of them is a bechor, not for inheritance and not for the Kohen.
chunks.st: both of them are not firstborn, neither with regard to inheritance nor with regard to redemption from a priest.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: the first is a bechor for inheritance,
chunks.st: The first son is a firstborn with regard to inheritance if he is his father’s first son,

chunks.en: and the second for the five sela'im.
chunks.st: and the second son is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest for five sela
chunks.stMore: coins, because he is the first to emerge from the womb and he emerged in the usual way.

mishnayos.summary: A man whose wife had twin boys as her first children gives the Kohen five sela'im. The mishnah teaches what happens if one twin or the father dies.

chunks.en: A man whose wife never had a child before
chunks.st: With regard to one whose wife had not previously given birth

chunks.en: and she had two boys:
chunks.st: and then gave birth to two males,
chunks.stMore: i.e., twin males, and it is unknown which is the firstborn,

chunks.en: he gives five sela'im to the Kohen.
chunks.st: he gives five sela coins to the priest after thirty days have passed.

chunks.he: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: If one of them died within thirty days,
chunks.st: If one of them dies within thirty days
chunks.stMore: of birth, before the obligation to redeem the firstborn takes effect,

chunks.en: the father is free.
chunks.st: the father is exempt
chunks.stMore: from the payment due to uncertainty, as perhaps it was the firstborn who died.

chunks.en: If the father died and the sons are alive,
chunks.st: In a case where the father died and the sons are alive,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: אִם נָתְנוּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָלְקוּ, נָתָנוּ.
chunks.en: if they gave before they split up the property, they gave.
chunks.st: If they gave the five sela coins to the priest before they divided their father’s property between them, they gave
chunks.stMore: it, and it remains in the possession of the priest.

chunks.en: But if not, they are free.
chunks.st: But if not, they are exempt
chunks.stMore: from giving the redemption money to the priest.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says, the property already owes it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: The obligation to redeem the firstborn already took effect on the property
chunks.stMore: of the father; therefore, in either case the sons, his heirs, are required to pay the priest.

chunks.en: A boy and a girl:
chunks.st: If the wife gave birth to a male and a female and it is not known which was born first,

chunks.en: the Kohen gets nothing here.
chunks.st: the priest has nothing here,
chunks.stMore: as it is possible that the female was born first.

mishnayos.summary: A man has two wives, and both have their first babies at the same time, and the babies get mixed up. The mishnah teaches how much he gives the Kohen.

chunks.en: Two wives who never had children before
chunks.st: With regard to two wives of one man, both of whom had not previously given birth,

chunks.en: had two boys:
chunks.st: and they gave birth to two males,
chunks.stMore: i.e., each bore one male, and the sons were intermingled, the father

chunks.en: he gives ten sela'im to the Kohen.
chunks.st: gives ten sela coins to the priest
chunks.stMore: even if it is unknown which son was born first, because it is certain that each is firstborn of his mother.

chunks.he: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: If one of them died within thirty days:
chunks.st: In a case where one of them dies within thirty days of birth,

chunks.en: if he gave to one Kohen,
chunks.st: if he gave all ten sela coins to one priest,

chunks.en: the Kohen gives him back five sela'im.
chunks.st: the priest must return five sela to him,
chunks.stMore: because the father was not obligated to redeem the son who then died.

chunks.en: If he gave to two Kohanim,
chunks.st: And if he gave the redemption payment to two different priests,

chunks.en: he cannot take it back from them.
chunks.st: he cannot reclaim the money from the possession
chunks.stMore: of either priest, as each could claim that the money that he received was for the living child.

chunks.he: זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה אוֹ שְׁנֵי זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבָה,
chunks.en: A boy and a girl, or two boys and a girl:
chunks.st: If one mother gave birth to a male and one gave birth to a female, or if between them they gave birth to two males and one female, and the children were intermingled,

chunks.en: he gives five sela'im to the Kohen.
chunks.st: the father gives five sela coins to the priest:
chunks.stMore: In the first case because the male might have preceded the female and in the second case because one of the males is certainly firstborn.

chunks.en: Two girls and a boy,
chunks.st: If the children were two females and a male,

chunks.en: or two boys and two girls:
chunks.st: or two males and two females,

chunks.en: the Kohen gets nothing here.
chunks.st: the priest has nothing here,
chunks.stMore: as it is possible the female was born first to each mother.

chunks.en: If one wife had a child before
chunks.st: If one of his wives had previously given birth

chunks.en: and one did not,
chunks.st: and one had not previously given birth

chunks.en: and they had two boys:
chunks.st: and they gave birth to two males who became intermingled,

chunks.en: he gives five sela'im to the Kohen.
chunks.st: the father gives five sela coins to the priest,
chunks.stMore: as it is certain that one of them was born to the mother who had not yet given birth.

chunks.he: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: If one of them died within thirty days,
chunks.st: If one of them dies within thirty days of birth

chunks.en: the father is free.
chunks.st: the father is exempt
chunks.stMore: from that payment, as it is possible that the one who died was born to the mother who had not yet given birth.

chunks.en: If the father died and the sons are alive,
chunks.st: In a case of intermingling where the father died and the sons are alive,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: אִם נָתְנוּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָלְקוּ, נָתָנוּ.
chunks.en: if they gave before they split up the property, they gave.
chunks.st: If they gave the five sela coins to the priest before they divided their father’s property between them, they gave
chunks.stMore: it, and it remains in the possession of the priest.

chunks.en: But if not, they are free.
chunks.st: But if not, they are exempt
chunks.stMore: from giving the redemption payment to the priest.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: the property already owes it.
chunks.st: The obligation to redeem the firstborn already took effect on the property of the father.

chunks.en: A boy and a girl:
chunks.st: If the wives gave birth to a male and a female

chunks.en: the Kohen gets nothing here.
chunks.st: the priest has nothing here,
chunks.stMore: as perhaps the female was born to the mother who had not yet given birth.

mishnayos.summary: Two wives of two different men have their first babies, and the babies get mixed up. If it is a boy and a girl, the boy must redeem himself when he grows up.

chunks.en: Two wives of two men
chunks.st: With regard to two women who had not previously given birth, who were married to two different men,

chunks.en: who never had children before had two boys:
chunks.st: and they gave birth to two males and the sons were intermingled,

chunks.en: this one gives five sela'im to the Kohen,
chunks.st: this father gives five sela coins to a priest

chunks.en: and that one gives five sela'im to the Kohen.
chunks.st: and that father gives five sela
chunks.stMore: coins to a priest, as each is certainly firstborn to his mother.

chunks.he: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: If one of them died within thirty days:
chunks.st: In a case where one of them dies within thirty days of birth,

chunks.en: if they gave to one Kohen,
chunks.st: if the fathers gave all ten sela coins to one priest,

chunks.en: he gives them back five sela'im.
chunks.st: the priest must return five sela coins to them.

chunks.en: If they gave to two Kohanim,
chunks.st: But if they gave the redemption payment to two different priests

chunks.en: they cannot take it back from them.
chunks.st: they cannot reclaim the money from the possession of
chunks.stMore: either priest, as each could claim that the money that he received was for the living child.

chunks.en: A boy and a girl:
chunks.st: If the women gave birth to a male and a female and the children became intermingled,

chunks.en: the fathers are free,
chunks.st: the fathers are exempt,
chunks.stMore: as each could claim that he is the father of the female,

chunks.en: and the son must redeem himself.
chunks.st: but the son is obligated to redeem himself, as he is certainly a firstborn.

chunks.en: Two girls and a boy,
chunks.st: If two females and a male were born,

chunks.en: or two boys and two girls:
chunks.st: or two females and two males,

chunks.en: the Kohen gets nothing here.
chunks.st: the priest has nothing here,
chunks.stMore: as it is possible the female was born first to each mother.

mishnayos.summary: More cases of pidyon haben: what if the baby dies, what if the father dies, and who is redeemed first, a father or his son.

chunks.en: If one wife had a child before
chunks.st: If one woman had previously given birth

chunks.en: and one did not,
chunks.st: and one had not previously given birth,

chunks.en: and they belong to two men,
chunks.st: and they were married to two men

chunks.en: and they had two boys:
chunks.st: and they gave birth to two males, who then became intermingled,

chunks.en: the one whose wife never had a child before
chunks.st: this one whose wife had not previously given birth

chunks.en: gives five sela'im to the Kohen.
chunks.st: gives five sela coins to the priest.

chunks.en: A boy and a girl:
chunks.st: If the women gave birth to a male and a female

chunks.en: the Kohen gets nothing here.
chunks.st: the priest has nothing here,
chunks.stMore: as it is possible the female was born to the mother who had not yet given birth.

chunks.en: If the son died within thirty days,
chunks.st: If the firstborn son dies within thirty days of birth,

chunks.en: even though he gave to the Kohen,
chunks.st: although the father gave five sela to the priest,

chunks.en: the Kohen gives back the five sela'im.
chunks.st: the priest must return it.

chunks.en: After thirty days,
chunks.st: If the firstborn son dies after thirty days have passed,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן, יִתֵּן.
chunks.en: even though he did not give, he must give.
chunks.st: even if the father did not give five sela coins to the priest he must give it then.

chunks.en: If he died on the thirtieth day, it is like the day before.
chunks.st: If the firstborn dies on the thirtieth day, that day’s halakhic status is like that of the day that preceded it,
chunks.stMore: as the obligation takes effect only after thirty days have elapsed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.stMore: If the firstborn dies on the thirtieth day it is a case of uncertainty; therefore,

chunks.en: if he gave,
chunks.st: if the father already gave the redemption payment to the priest

chunks.en: he does not take it back,
chunks.st: he cannot take it back,

chunks.en: and if he did not give,
chunks.st: but if he did not yet give payment

chunks.en: he does not give.
chunks.st: he does not need to give it.

chunks.en: If the father died within thirty days,
chunks.st: If the father of the firstborn dies within thirty days of birth

chunks.en: we treat the son as not redeemed
chunks.st: the presumptive status of the son is that he was not redeemed,

chunks.en: until he brings proof that he was redeemed.
chunks.st: until the son will bring proof that he was redeemed.

chunks.en: After thirty days,
chunks.st: If the father dies after thirty days have passed

chunks.en: we treat him as redeemed,
chunks.st: the presumptive status of the son is that he was redeemed,

chunks.en: until people say he was not redeemed.
chunks.st: until people will tell him that he was not redeemed.

chunks.en: If a man needs to be redeemed and his son needs to be redeemed,
chunks.st: If one had both himself to redeem and his son to redeem,

chunks.en: he comes before his son.
chunks.st: his own redemption takes precedence over that of his son.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: his son comes first,
chunks.st: The redemption of his son takes precedence,

chunks.en: because his own mitzvah was on his father,
chunks.st: as the mitzva to redeem the father is incumbent upon his own father,

chunks.en: and the mitzvah of his son is on him.
chunks.st: and the mitzva to redeem his son is incumbent upon him.

mishnayos.summary: The money the Torah sets for pidyon haben and for some other payments is counted in holy shekels, using the coins of Tzor.

chunks.en: The five sela'im for a son
are in the coins of Tzor.

words.note: Tzor's silver coins were pure and heavy.

chunks.en: The thirty paid for a slave,
and the fifty paid by a man who did wrong to a girl,
and the hundred paid by one who spreads a false bad name,
all of them are in the holy shekel,
in the coins of Tzor.
And they all may be paid with money
or with things worth money,
except for the shekalim.

words.note: The half-shekel each Jew gave every year to the Beis HaMikdash.

mishnayos.summary: What may be used to pay for pidyon haben, and what happens if the father writes a note, or loses the money he set aside.
